Starlink Mini USB-C power requirements

The Starlink Mini can run from a USB-C PD (Power Delivery) power source, but it needs more than a typical phone charger.

Specification

	

Requirement




USB-C protocol

	

USB Power Delivery (PD)




Minimum PD output

	

100W (20V ⎓ 5A)




Recommended charger

	

100W or higher




Typical power consumption

	

25–40W




USB-C cable

	

5A-rated, e-marked cable




Connector

	

Starlink Mini USB-C-to-barrel-jack power cable

Important: The Starlink Mini doesn't have a native USB-C input. You need a compatible USB-C PD-to-DC power cable.

A 65W USB-C charger generally isn't sufficient for the official USB-C power setup, even though the Mini typically consumes much less than 65W.

Why 100W if the Mini only uses 25–40W?

The 100W rating is the required capability of the USB-C PD source, not the Mini's continuous consumption. Starlink specifies 100W to support reliable operation, including startup and peak loads. 
Starlink Help Center
+1

For a power bank, make sure one USB-C port supports 20V/5A. A power bank advertised as 100W total across multiple ports may not qualify.

Official references: Starlink Mini power requirements and Official USB-C cable specifications.
